title: KV fragmentation surgeon: continuous micro-defrag + batch alignment
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
GPU-resident KV cache suffers gradual fragmentation under mixed workload traffic: repeated insert/evict churn leaves many small holes that reduce usable capacity and force premature evictions, increasing token fetches and tail latency. Continuous batching amplifies the issue because batch alignment groups requests with overlapping token residency patterns, which can both help (reuse) and hurt (concentrate fragmentation).

Goal:
Design and deliver a low-risk on-GPU allocation + micro-defragmentation strategy that: 1) reduces effective fragmentation and usable-memory loss by >=10% on steady-state mixed workloads, 2) maintains P99 token fetch latency within current SLOs (no more than +5% regression), 3) integrates with continuous batching (no blocking global pauses), and 4) exposes telemetry for tuning and rollouts.

Proposed solution ("Fragmentation Surgeon") summary:
- Allocation: introduce a lightweight two-tier allocator: small "micro-slab" pools for short-lived KV entries and larger "stripe-slab" pools for long-residency KV. Allocation decision uses an online residency predictor (LRU+age histogram) informed by recent batch-access patterns.
- Batch alignment: when forming micro-batches, tag requests with residency fingerprints; if a batch contains high overlap, preferentially allocate from co-located slab stripes to increase cache reuse and make future locality-aware compaction easier.
- Continuous micro-defrag: background on-GPU defrag worker that performs bounded-size copy/relocate operations (micro-migrations) during low-GPU-util windows. Micro-migrations are scheduled in alignment with batching slack windows so they avoid increasing tail latency.
- Indirection layer and safepoint migration: use a compact indirection table (GPU L1-friendly) enabling relocation without updating upstream request paths; migrations become atomic pointer swaps at safepoints. Safepoints are coordinated with the batching runtime to avoid KV reads mid-relocation.
- Eviction-aware compaction: prefer compacting regions that yield largest contiguous free span relative to expected future batch overlap.
- Telemetry & rollout: add fragmentation heatmaps, micro-migration counts, migration cost histograms, and allocation-class occupancy metrics to Console per-model dashboards.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Slight memory overhead (~1-3%) for indirection table and micro-scratch space; justified by effective capacity recovered from fragmentation.
- Micro-migrations increase GPU bandwidth; we throttle worker based on observed batch latency to avoid regressions.
- Residency predictor complexity kept minimal (histogram + decay) to avoid CPU-GPU sync overhead.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration test that simulates mixed traffic (chatty short sessions + long-context streaming) shows >=10% effective usable-memory gain or equal token eviction reduction at target throughput.
- P50/P95/P99 token fetch latencies remain within +/-5% of baseline under controlled load tests.
- Console surfaces fragmentation metrics and a per-model toggle to enable gradual rollout.
- PRs merged with tests, and no new flaky GPU CI failures introduced.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: enable surgeon in low-traffic cluster for 1 week, telemetry-only mode first (migrations logged but not applied).
2) Pilot: enable micro-migrations with strict throttle (<=5% bandwidth) for a single region and subset of models. 48hr observability window.
3) Gradual ramp: expand to 25% of capacity with adaptive throttle; run 7-day regression sweep.
4) Full: enable by default with opt-out config per-tenant.

Metrics to watch:
- Fragmentation ratio (free-fragments / free-total) by slab class
- Effective usable-memory (contiguous spans >= X bytes)
- Micro-migration count, bytes moved, average migration latency
- Token eviction rate and read-after-evict spikes
- Batch formation latency and end-to-end request P99

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Primary implementation in runtime/gpu/allocator.{cc,cu} and runtime/gpu/migration_worker.{cc,cu}
- Indirection table is kept in GPU global memory with a small L1 cache in shared memory for hot lookups.
- Migration worker uses persistent CUDA streams to avoid kernel launch latency spikes.
- Provide knobs via config: micro_migration_window_ms, max_bytes_per_window, residency_decay_half_life, enable_batch_colocation_alloc

Open questions for design review:
- How aggressive should residency prediction decay be for bursty (chatty) workloads? Empirically evaluate half-lives 1s/10s/60s.
- Should compacting prefer older slabs vs. high-churn slabs when both free similar total bytes?
- Coordination with dedicated autoscaling: migration worker should defer when autoscaler is actively reshaping GPU pools to avoid extra data movement.

comments: 2025-02-10 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after runtime triage; attached initial sim results showing ~14% loss in usable contiguous spans on mixed workloads.
2025-02-14 - Mateo Ruiz: Added allocation sketch and micro-migration algorithm; ran quick local GPU sim to validate pointer indirection overhead (~1.2% extra memory).

2025-02-20 - Design review: feedback from Lina Park and Noah Patel - prefer simpler residency predictor and explicit per-model opt-out. Action: remove ML predictor prototype; stick to histogram decay approach (Mateo).

2025-02-26 - Engineering sync: implemented prototype allocator and telemetry hooks. Observed a 6% regression in P99 under synthetic peak; root cause: migration worker not throttled. Patch #2 introduces adaptive throttle based on batch latency (PR linked).

2025-03-02 - QA: began long-run canary in lab cluster (8 GPUs) with mixed chat + streaming workload. Early signals: token eviction rate down 11%, fragmentation ratio reduced 18%, P99 within +3%. Continuing longer run.
2025-03-05 - PM review: approve pilot rollout. Need to finalize dashboard thresholds and add canary rollback automation.
